title: Toxicology Markers: Acetaminophen Levels, Cholinesterases, Blood Lead and Urine Cannabinoids
summary: Learn which specimen, marker and threshold each of four poisons needs: a timed serum acetaminophen concentration read against the nomogram treatment line, red cell acetylcholinesterase versus plasma butyrylcholinesterase after organophosphate exposure, whole blood lead against the CDC reference value, and urine cannabinoid and cocaine metabolite windows that belong to the cut-off rather than the drug.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 24 Hit 6 (acetaminophen dose threshold, NAPQI, timing of peak injury, N-acetylcysteine), Hit 10 (organophosphate confirmation by red cell acetylcholinesterase and plasma pseudocholinesterase), Hit 11 (lead measured in whole blood, measurement methods, action thresholds, basophilic stippling from pyrimidine-5-prime-nucleotidase inhibition) and Hit 12 (urinary cannabinoid detection window versus cocaine). Checked against Yoon 2016, Eddleston 2008, Ruckart 2021, Hu 2007, Kim 2015, Kosnett 2007 and Nickley 2017 (Europe PMC full text) and Goodwin 2008, Lowe 2009 and Valentine 1976 (Europe PMC abstracts only). Qualified against sources: the toxic-dose figure, the NAPQI fraction, the cholinesterase severity percentages, the 10 micrograms per decilitre childhood threshold and the two-day cocaine window all differ from the sources read — see register flags rv-apap-toxic-dose-150, rv-apap-napqi-fraction, rv-op-chol-severity-cutoffs, rv-lead-blrv-outdated, rv-lead-blrv-us-scope and rv-cocaine-window-cutoff-dependent. Not taught: the claim that THC has the longest window of the common drugs of abuse, the ~1 week chronic-user half-life, the 32-year bone half-life, the 96% skeletal body burden, and the >25 micrograms per decilitre paediatric chelation figure, none of which the sources read state.

objectives: Choose the right specimen and marker for acetaminophen, organophosphate, lead and urine cannabinoid testing.
Use a timed serum acetaminophen concentration rather than a reported dose to decide on N-acetylcysteine.
Separate red cell acetylcholinesterase (severity) from plasma butyrylcholinesterase (exposure) and handle the sample correctly.
State what the CDC blood lead reference value is, and why a urine drug detection window depends on the cut-off.

scenes.title: Four requests, four wrong tubes
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: four toxicology requests land together. (1) A 70-kg adult who says he swallowed about 10 g of acetaminophen four hours ago — the resident wants to decide on the antidote from the milligrams per kilogram alone. (2) A farm worker with pinpoint pupils and sweating — a plasma cholinesterase is ordered and the tube is left on the bench. (3) A 3-year-old with pica — a SERUM lead is ordered. (4) A urine cannabinoid screen that is positive, reported as "used in the last few days". Question token: "Right marker, right tube, right threshold?"

cues.text: Four toxicology requests land together. An adult who swallowed acetaminophen four hours ago, where the antidote decision is being made from milligrams per kilogram. A farm worker with pinpoint pupils, whose cholinesterase tube is left sitting on the bench.
A three-year-old with pica, for whom a serum lead has been ordered. And a positive urine cannabinoid screen, reported as use within the last few days.
Each request has the right idea and the wrong execution. Which marker, which tube, and which threshold does each one actually need?

props.label: 4 Urine cannabinoid + → "used in the last few days"
Right marker, right tube, right threshold?

scenes.title: What each marker actually measures
scenes.altText: Four schematic cards. Acetaminophen: about 10% of a dose is oxidised by CYP2E1 (less by 1A2 and 3A4) to the reactive metabolite NAPQI, normally conjugated by glutathione; when glucuronidation and sulfation saturate, more goes down the oxidative route and glutathione is depleted. The clinical measurement is a timed serum acetaminophen concentration. Cholinesterases: organophosphorus compounds inhibit acetylcholinesterase in synapses and on red cell membranes, and butyrylcholinesterase in plasma; red cell acetylcholinesterase is measured in whole blood with butyrylcholinesterase blocked by an inhibitor, because acetylcholinesterase is present at very low levels in plasma and serum. Lead: measured in whole blood drawn by venous phlebotomy or fingerstick into an anticoagulant tube, usually by graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy with a detection limit near 1 microgram per decilitre; some laboratories still use anodic stripping voltammetry with a detection limit near 5. Urine cannabinoids: immunoassay screens for the carboxy metabolite THCCOOH at a 50 nanogram per millilitre cut-off, confirmed by gas chromatography mass spectrometry after base hydrolysis.

cues.text: Start with what each marker is. About ten percent of an acetaminophen dose is oxidised by cytochrome P450 2E1 to the reactive metabolite NAPQI, which glutathione normally mops up. Saturate the conjugation routes and more goes down the oxidative one.

Organophosphorus compounds inhibit acetylcholinesterase in synapses and on red cell membranes, and butyrylcholinesterase in plasma. Red cell acetylcholinesterase is assayed in whole blood with the plasma enzyme blocked, because acetylcholinesterase is barely present in plasma.

Lead is measured in whole blood, drawn into an anticoagulant tube, most often by graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy, with a detection limit near one microgram per decilitre. Anodic stripping voltammetry, still used in some laboratories, reaches about five.
Urine cannabinoid screens do not look for the drug. They look for the carboxy metabolite at a fifty nanogram per millilitre cut-off, confirmed by mass spectrometry after hydrolysis.

scenes.title: The thresholds that moved
scenes.altText: Four threshold cards. Acetaminophen: for a known acute single ingestion within 24 hours the decision comes from the timed serum concentration on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram, not from the reported dose. The probable toxicity line passes through 200 micrograms per millilitre at 4 hours and 25 at 16 hours; the United States, Australia and New Zealand use a treatment line starting at 150 at 4 hours, set 25% below the probable toxicity line deliberately, to absorb an inaccurate history and laboratory error. Ingestions causing hepatic failure are usually in excess of 150 mg/kg, though lower doses have caused injury. Organophosphates: red cell acetylcholinesterase of at least 30% of normal came with normal muscle function and no need for atropine; below 10% of normal came with grossly deranged muscle function and high atropine requirements; in between, moderate impairment. Plasma butyrylcholinesterase activity does not track severity at all — it is a sensitive marker of exposure and of elimination, recovering about 7% of normal per day once the compound has gone. Lead: the CDC blood lead reference value was updated in 2021 from 5 to 3.5 micrograms per decilitre, the 97.5th percentile for United States children aged 1 to 5 years; it is a population percentile, explicitly not a health-based standard or a toxicity threshold. Ten micrograms per decilitre was the 1991 level of concern. Cannabinoids and cocaine: the window belongs to the cut-off, not the drug.

cues.text: Now the numbers, and how they move. For a known acute acetaminophen ingestion inside twenty-four hours, the antidote decision comes from a timed serum concentration on the nomogram, not from the reported dose. The probable toxicity line runs through two hundred micrograms per millilitre at four hours.

The United States, Australia and New Zealand treat from a lower line, one hundred and fifty at four hours, set a quarter below the probable toxicity line on purpose, to absorb a wrong history and laboratory error. Doses causing hepatic failure are usually above one hundred and fifty milligrams per kilogram, but lower ones have injured livers too.

For organophosphates the two enzymes answer different questions. Red cell acetylcholinesterase at thirty percent of normal or more came with normal muscle function and no atropine; under ten percent came with grossly deranged muscle function and high atropine doses. Plasma butyrylcholinesterase does not track severity at all: it marks exposure, and recovers about seven percent of normal a day once the compound is gone.

And for lead the reference value moved. The CDC blood lead reference value fell from five to three point five micrograms per decilitre in twenty twenty-one. It is the ninety-seven point five percentile for United States children aged one to five, a population percentile, not a toxicity threshold. Ten was the nineteen ninety-one level of concern.

scenes.title: Pre-analytics, and what a positive proves
scenes.altText: Pre-analytical cards. Cholinesterase: the reaction between the organophosphorus compound, acetylcholinesterase and any oxime continues in the tube at room temperature, so the sample must be diluted and cooled immediately; one group dilutes twenty-fold at the bedside into cold saline and freezes within five minutes. Lead: fingerstick specimens are often contaminated by environmental lead, so venous sampling is less likely to be contaminated and follow-up testing to confirm is recommended; federal proficiency testing criteria are plus or minus 4 micrograms per decilitre or 10%, whichever is greater. Detection windows: under continuously monitored abstinence, mean days to the last positive urine cannabinoid screen were 4.3, 9.7 and 15.4 days for creatinine-corrected starting concentrations of 0 to 50, 51 to 150 and above 150 nanograms per milligram; one heavy chronic user stayed positive at least 24 days. For cocaine, a 5 nanogram per millilitre benzoylecgonine cut-off gave a detection window of 17 to 22 days, against the usual 100 nanogram per millilitre industry cut-off. Hook answers: (1) timed serum level against the treatment line; (2) red cell acetylcholinesterase, chilled at once; (3) whole blood lead, venous; (4) a positive screen does not date the use.

cues.text: Pre-analytics decide two of these. In the cholinesterase tube the reaction between the pesticide, the enzyme and any oxime keeps going at room temperature, so a few minutes on the bench changes the answer. The sample must be diluted and chilled immediately.

For lead, fingerstick specimens are often contaminated by environmental lead, so venous sampling is cleaner and confirmatory follow-up testing is recommended. Federal proficiency criteria allow four micrograms per decilitre or ten percent, whichever is larger.

Detection windows belong to the cut-off. Under monitored abstinence, mean days to the last positive cannabinoid screen were four, ten and fifteen days depending on the starting concentration, and one heavy user stayed positive at least twenty-four days. Drop the cocaine metabolite cut-off from a hundred to five nanograms per millilitre and the window stretches to seventeen to twenty-two days.

So, the hook. A timed serum level against the treatment line. Red cell acetylcholinesterase, chilled at once. Whole blood lead, drawn from a vein. And a positive urine screen that cannot date the use.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards. "A dose in mg/kg decides the antidote" (dodge: for a known acute single ingestion the timed serum concentration on the nomogram decides; the treatment line is deliberately set low because histories and assays are imperfect). "Plasma cholinesterase grades how sick the patient is" (dodge: butyrylcholinesterase does not track severity; red cell acetylcholinesterase does, and the sample must be chilled at once). "A blood lead of 4 micrograms per decilitre is normal because the cut-off is 10" (dodge: the CDC reference value is 3.5 micrograms per decilitre since 2021, and it is a population percentile, not a safe level).

cues.text: Trap one: the milligrams per kilogram decide the antidote. No. For a known acute single ingestion, the timed serum concentration on the nomogram decides, and the treatment line sits low on purpose because histories and assays are imperfect.

Trap two: plasma cholinesterase tells you how sick the patient is. No. Butyrylcholinesterase marks exposure, not severity, and the red cell enzyme is the one that tracks severity, if the tube was chilled at once.
Trap three: a blood lead of four is normal because the cut-off is ten. No. The reference value has been three point five since twenty twenty-one, and it is a population percentile, not a safe level.

scenes.title: Four witnesses
scenes.altText: Memory aid: "Four poisons, four witnesses. Acetaminophen is testified to by a CLOCK (a timed serum level). The organophosphate is testified to by an ENZYME still working (red cell acetylcholinesterase activity). Lead is testified to by the WHOLE BLOOD in the tube. Cannabis is testified to by a CUT-OFF, and a cut-off cannot say when." A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: four poisons, four witnesses. Acetaminophen is testified to by a clock, a timed serum level. The organophosphate by an enzyme still working, the red cell acetylcholinesterase. Lead by the whole blood in the tube. And cannabis by a cut-off, which can never say when.

Where it breaks: cholinesterase results rarely come back in time to change treatment, so the diagnosis stays clinical; the blood lead reference value is a population percentile, not a toxicity threshold, and blood lead does not measure accumulated body burden; and a negative acetaminophen level does not prove no injury, because the drug can clear while the liver is already hurt.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: A negative APAP level ≠ no injury

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: "APAP: timed serum level vs treatment line · OP: RBC AChE severity, plasma BChE exposure", "Lead: whole blood, reference value 3.5 µg/dL · urine cannabinoid window belongs to the cut-off".

cues.text: Each poison has its own right measurement: acetaminophen needs a timed serum concentration read against the treatment line, organophosphates need red cell acetylcholinesterase for severity and plasma butyrylcholinesterase for exposure, lead needs whole blood, and a urine cannabinoid result means only what its cut-off allows.

props.label: APAP: timed level vs treat line · OP: RBC AChE = severity, BChE = exposure
Lead: whole blood, reference value 3.5 µg/dL · cannabinoid window = the cut-off

explanation.what: Plain language: four poisons, four different right answers about what to put in the tube and which number to compare it with. Acetaminophen is judged by a blood level taken at a known time, not by how much the patient says they swallowed. Organophosphate pesticides are judged by how much enzyme activity is left, and there are two enzymes that answer two different questions. Lead is judged in whole blood. A urine cannabis result is judged against a cut-off that decides how far back the test can see. Scientific terms: N-acetyl-para-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI), cytochrome P450 2E1, glutathione, Rumack-Matthew nomogram, probable toxicity line, treatment line, N-acetylcysteine (NAC), acetylcholinesterase (AChE), butyrylcholinesterase (BChE, plasma or pseudocholinesterase), oxime, blood lead level (BLL), blood lead reference value (BLRV), graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy (GFAAS), anodic stripping voltammetry (ASV), K-shell X-ray fluorescence (KXRF), pyrimidine-5-prime-nucleotidase, 11-nor-9-carboxy-tetrahydrocannabinol (THCCOOH), benzoylecgonine.
explanation.why: Each marker sits at a different point in the poisoning. A timed acetaminophen level predicts hepatotoxicity before the liver is injured, which is why a conservative treatment line is used. Enzyme activity reflects how much target the pesticide has already hit, and the two cholinesterases differ in what they reflect and how fast they come back. Blood lead reflects recent exposure plus lead mobilised from stores rather than total body burden, and its interpretive value is a shifting population percentile. A urine metabolite result reflects accumulated excretion, so its time reach is set by the assay cut-off.
explanation.measure: Acetaminophen: about 10% of a dose is oxidised by CYP2E1 to NAPQI; for a known acute single ingestion within 24 hours plot the timed serum concentration on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram. The probable toxicity line passes through 200 micrograms per millilitre at 4 hours and 25 at 16 hours; the United States, Australia and New Zealand treat from a line starting at 150 at 4 hours, 25% lower by design. Ingestions causing hepatic failure are usually above 150 mg/kg. Maximal liver injury falls in stage III, 72 to 96 hours after ingestion. Oral NAC is 140 mg/kg loading then 70 mg/kg every 4 hours for 18 doses. Organophosphates: red cell AChE activity of at least 30% of normal came with normal muscle function and no atropine requirement, under 10% with grossly deranged muscle function and high atropine doses, in between with moderate impairment; plasma BChE does not track severity but is a sensitive exposure marker and recovers about 7% of normal per day. Lead: whole blood, venous phlebotomy or fingerstick into an anticoagulant tube, GFAAS with a detection limit near 1 microgram per decilitre, ASV near 5; the CDC blood lead reference value is 3.5 micrograms per decilitre since 2021 (97.5th percentile for children aged 1 to 5 years), replacing 5 (2012) and 10 (1991 level of concern). Urine cannabinoids: immunoassay cut-off 50 nanograms per millilitre with mass spectrometric confirmation; mean days to last positive were 4.3, 9.7 and 15.4 for creatinine-corrected starting concentrations of 0 to 50, 51 to 150 and above 150 nanograms per milligram, and at least 24 days in one heavy chronic user. Cocaine: at a 5 nanogram per millilitre benzoylecgonine cut-off the window was 17 to 22 days, against a usual industry cut-off of 100.
explanation.differs: Reported dose versus timed serum concentration; probable toxicity line versus treatment line; red cell AChE (severity, whole blood, slow recovery) versus plasma BChE (exposure, faster recovery, no severity information); whole blood lead (recent exposure plus mobilised stores) versus cortical bone lead by KXRF (cumulative dose over decades); a screening cut-off versus a confirmation cut-off, which is what sets a detection window.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: pick what decides N-acetylcysteine after an acute ingestion, pick which cholinesterase grades severity, pick the correct specimen or handling for a cholinesterase or lead request, or decide whether a positive urine cannabinoid screen can date the last use.

mnemonic.text: Four poisons, four witnesses: acetaminophen is testified to by a CLOCK (a timed serum level), the organophosphate by an ENZYME still working (red cell acetylcholinesterase activity), lead by the WHOLE BLOOD in the tube, and cannabis by a CUT-OFF — and a cut-off can never say when.
mnemonic.explanation: Ties each poison to the specimen or property that actually carries the information.
mnemonic.limitation: Cholinesterase results rarely return in time to change treatment, so organophosphate diagnosis stays clinical; the blood lead reference value is a population percentile rather than a toxicity threshold, and blood lead does not measure accumulated body burden; and a negative acetaminophen level does not prove absence of injury, because the drug can clear while the liver is already damaged.

analogyLimitations: Metabolism, enzymes and detection windows are drawn as schematic cards, not real data plots.
The cannabinoid and cocaine day figures come from small controlled-abstinence and monitored-patient studies and vary with the assay cut-off.
takeaway: Each poison has its own right measurement: acetaminophen needs a timed serum concentration read against the treatment line, organophosphates need red cell acetylcholinesterase for severity and plasma butyrylcholinesterase for exposure, lead needs whole blood, and a urine cannabinoid result means only what its cut-off allows.

questions.stem: A 70-kg adult presents 4 hours after a single acetaminophen ingestion and reports swallowing about 10 g. Which result should decide whether N-acetylcysteine is started?

options.text: The serum acetaminophen concentration at 4 hours, plotted against the nomogram treatment line
options.rationale: Correct. For a known acute single ingestion within 24 hours the timed serum concentration is plotted on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram, and the treatment line begins at 150 micrograms per millilitre at 4 hours.

options.text: The reported dose in mg/kg alone
options.rationale: Incorrect. The treatment line was deliberately set 25% below the probable toxicity line precisely because the ingestion history and the assay are both imperfect, and injury has been reported below the usual dose threshold.

options.text: The peak alanine aminotransferase, measured at 72 hours
options.rationale: Incorrect. Maximal liver injury falls in stage III, 72 to 96 hours after ingestion, so waiting for it forfeits the window in which the antidote works best.

options.text: A repeat acetaminophen concentration at 24 hours
options.rationale: Incorrect. A concentration that late cannot be read on the nomogram for this ingestion, and the delay removes the benefit of early treatment.

questions.stem: A farm worker is admitted with suspected organophosphate poisoning. Which statement about the cholinesterase assays is correct?

options.text: Red cell acetylcholinesterase reflects severity, while plasma butyrylcholinesterase is a sensitive marker of exposure
options.rationale: Correct. Activity of at least 30% of normal red cell acetylcholinesterase came with normal muscle function and no atropine requirement and under 10% with grossly deranged function, whereas butyrylcholinesterase activity does not relate to severity but marks exposure and elimination.

options.text: Plasma butyrylcholinesterase activity grades how severely the patient is poisoned
options.rationale: Incorrect. Butyrylcholinesterase activity does not relate to the severity of poisoning, and many of these compounds inhibit it more than they inhibit acetylcholinesterase.

options.text: Acetylcholinesterase is best measured in serum, since that is where it circulates
options.rationale: Incorrect. Acetylcholinesterase is present at very low levels in human plasma and serum; it is measured in whole blood with butyrylcholinesterase blocked by an inhibitor.

options.text: The specimen can sit at room temperature until the batch is run, because the enzyme is stable
options.rationale: Incorrect. The reaction between the compound, the enzyme and any oxime continues in the tube, so the sample must be diluted and cooled immediately or repeated results vary.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old with pica has a venous whole blood lead of 4.2 micrograms per decilitre. Which interpretation matches current CDC guidance?

options.text: It is at or above the blood lead reference value of 3.5 micrograms per decilitre, which is a population percentile and not a toxicity threshold
options.rationale: Correct. CDC updated the reference value to 3.5 micrograms per decilitre in 2021 as the 97.5th percentile for children aged 1 to 5 years, and states explicitly that it is not a health-based standard or toxicity threshold.

options.text: It is well below the current threshold of 10 micrograms per decilitre, so no follow-up is needed
options.rationale: Incorrect. Ten micrograms per decilitre was the 1991 level of concern; the reference value has since moved to 5 in 2012 and 3.5 in 2021.

options.text: It meets the threshold for starting chelation therapy
options.rationale: Incorrect. Chelation of asymptomatic people with low blood lead concentrations is not recommended, and chelation is generally not advised below 45 micrograms per decilitre in adults.

options.text: Serum rather than whole blood is the preferred specimen for confirming the result
options.rationale: Incorrect. Blood lead levels are measured in whole blood collected into an anticoagulant tube, and venous sampling is preferred because skin-prick specimens are often contaminated with environmental lead.

references.citation: Lowe RH, Abraham TT, Darwin WD, Herning R, Cadet JL, Huestis MA. Extended urinary Delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol excretion in chronic cannabis users precludes use as a biomarker of new drug exposure. Drug Alcohol Depend. 2009;105(1-2):24-32. doi:10.1016/j.drugalcdep.2009.05.027
references.usedFor: Abstract only (the Europe PMC full text is not available for this author manuscript). Urinary THCCOOH is the usual marker of cannabis exposure although last use may have been weeks earlier in chronic users; in 33 chronic smokers under monitored abstinence, 11-hydroxy-THC and THCCOOH were detectable in one heavy chronic user for at least 24 days, and urinary THC and 11-hydroxy-THC are therefore not valid markers of recent use.

references.citation: Nickley J, Pesce AJ, Krock K. A sensitive assay for urinary cocaine metabolite benzoylecgonine shows more positive results and longer half-lives than those using traditional cut-offs. Drug Test Anal. 2017;9(8):1214-1216. doi:10.1002/dta.2153
references.usedFor: Read as Europe PMC full text. Lowering the benzoylecgonine cut-off from the typical industry 100 nanograms per millilitre to 5 nanograms per millilitre changed the observed window of detection after cessation of use to 17 to 22 days; single-dose studies had supported elimination within a few days, and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is cited as stating detection up to 10 days after a cocaine binge; apparent half-lives varied from 11 to 140 hours within the same patient.

references.citation: Valentine WN, Paglia DE, Fink K, Madokoro G. Lead poisoning: association with hemolytic anemia, basophilic stippling, erythrocyte pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency, and intraerythrocytic accumulation of pyrimidines. J Clin Invest. 1976;58(4):926-932. doi:10.1172/JCI108545
references.usedFor: Abstract only (the Europe PMC full text endpoint returns a server error for this record). Lead intoxication is accompanied by an acquired deficiency of erythrocyte pyrimidine-specific 5-prime-nucleotidase, and when severe produces the haemolysis, marked basophilic stippling and intraerythrocytic pyrimidine nucleotide accumulation seen in the inherited enzyme deficiency.

claims.text: About 10% of an acetaminophen dose is oxidised by CYP2E1 to NAPQI, normally conjugated by glutathione; saturation of conjugation drives the oxidative route.

For a known acute single ingestion within 24 hours the timed serum concentration on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram decides treatment; probable toxicity line 200 micrograms per millilitre at 4 h, United States treatment line 150 at 4 h, set 25% lower on purpose.
Ingestions causing hepatic failure usually exceed 150 mg/kg though lower doses have injured; maximal liver injury falls 72 to 96 hours after ingestion; N-acetylcysteine is the antidote.

Red cell acetylcholinesterase marks synaptic function and severity (at least 30% of normal, no atropine need; under 10%, grossly deranged function); plasma butyrylcholinesterase marks exposure and elimination, not severity, recovering about 7% per day.

Acetylcholinesterase is measured in whole blood with butyrylcholinesterase blocked because plasma levels are very low, and the sample must be diluted and cooled immediately because the reaction continues in the tube.

Lead is measured in whole blood collected into an anticoagulant tube by graphite furnace atomic absorption spectroscopy (limit near 1 microgram per decilitre) or anodic stripping voltammetry (near 5); hair and urine lead add little beyond blood lead; venous collection avoids skin-prick contamination.

The CDC blood lead reference value is 3.5 micrograms per decilitre since 2021 (97.5th percentile, children aged 1 to 5 years), replacing 5 in 2012 and the 1991 level of concern of 10, and is not a toxicity threshold.
Blood lead reflects recent exposure plus mobilised stores and not accumulated body burden; cortical bone lead by K-shell X-ray fluorescence reflects cumulative dose.
Lead inhibits pyrimidine-5-prime-nucleotidase, producing basophilic stippling and haemolysis; stippling is not specific to lead.

Urine cannabinoid immunoassay screens THCCOOH at 50 nanograms per millilitre; mean days to last positive were 4.3, 9.7 and 15.4 by starting concentration group, with at least 24 days in one heavy chronic user, so a positive cannot date the last use.
Lowering the benzoylecgonine cut-off from 100 to 5 nanograms per millilitre extended the observed detection window to 17 to 22 days, so a detection window is a property of the cut-off and method.
Chelation is not recommended for asymptomatic people with low blood lead, and generally not below 45 micrograms per decilitre in adults.
That THC has the longest urinary detection window of the common drugs of abuse, and that its half-life is about one week in chronic users.
claims.note: No source read compares windows across the common drugs of abuse or gives a chronic-user half-life; not taught.

claims.text: That cocaine is undetectable in urine after about 2 days.
claims.note: Nickley 2017 observed 17 to 22 days at a 5 nanograms per millilitre cut-off and cites detection up to 10 days after a binge; the 2-day figure is not taught.

claims.text: That the bone half-life of lead is 32 years and that 96% of the body burden sits in the skeleton.
claims.note: The sources read describe cortical bone as a long-term store without these figures; not taught.

claims.text: That a blood lead above 25 micrograms per decilitre prompts chelation in children.
claims.note: Only adult thresholds were found in the sources read; the paediatric figure is not taught.

claims.text: That 30 to 50% of normal cholinesterase indicates exposure, that more than 50% inhibition indicates toxic manifestations, and that symptoms may not appear until activity is at or below 20% of normal.
claims.note: Eddleston 2008 gives different bands for red cell acetylcholinesterase and states that plasma enzyme activity does not track severity; the reviewer percentages are not taught.

claims.text: The four-request scenario is invented and all diagrams are schematic cards.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 24 Hit 6 gives an acute toxic dose of 140 mg/kg. Yoon 2016 states that ingestions causing hepatic failure are usually in excess of 150 mg/kg, that lower doses have caused injury, and that treatment after a known acute ingestion is decided from the timed serum concentration against the nomogram treatment line rather than from the reported dose; 140 mg/kg is the oral N-acetylcysteine loading dose in the same review. The lesson teaches the level-based decision (register flag rv-apap-toxic-dose-150).

Ch. 24 Hit 6 says about 5% of the dose becomes NAPQI. Yoon 2016 states that about 10% of acetaminophen is shunted by CYP2E1 to NAPQI; the lesson teaches about 10% (register flag rv-apap-napqi-fraction).

Ch. 24 Hit 10 gives 30 to 50% of normal as exposure, more than 50% inhibition as toxic manifestations and symptoms appearing at or below 20% of normal, and calls plasma pseudocholinesterase sensitive. Eddleston 2008 states that plasma butyrylcholinesterase activity does not relate to severity at all and gives red cell acetylcholinesterase bands of at least 30% (no atropine need) and under 10% (grossly deranged function). The lesson teaches the source bands and the exposure-versus-severity split (register flag rv-op-chol-severity-cutoffs).

Ch. 24 Hit 11 says a blood lead of at least 10 micrograms per decilitre means excessive absorption in children. Ruckart 2021 records 10 as the 1991 level of concern, superseded by a reference value of 5 in 2012 and 3.5 in 2021; the lesson teaches 3.5 and its meaning as a population percentile (register flag rv-lead-blrv-outdated).

The blood lead reference value taught here is a United States CDC value derived from United States survey data. Philippine blood lead screening and action thresholds are not covered by the sources read, so candidates sitting a Philippine examination should check local rules (register flag rv-lead-blrv-us-scope).

Ch. 24 Hit 11 and the Number Vault say cocaine is gone from urine in about 2 days. Nickley 2017 observed a 17 to 22 day window at a 5 nanograms per millilitre benzoylecgonine cut-off and cites detection up to 10 days after a binge, so the window depends on the cut-off and method; the lesson teaches that (register flag rv-cocaine-window-cutoff-dependent).

morphology.note: No images; metabolism, enzyme activity bands, thresholds and detection windows are shown as cards and tokens.

verification.notes: All 12 taught factual claims are checked against Yoon 2016, Eddleston 2008, Ruckart 2021, Hu 2007, Kim 2015, Kosnett 2007 and Nickley 2017 (read as Europe PMC full text) and Goodwin 2008, Lowe 2009 and Valentine 1976 (Europe PMC abstracts only, so only what those abstracts state is taught). Five reviewer claims remain pending and are not taught: THC as the longest window among the common drugs of abuse and its chronic-user half-life, the 2-day cocaine window, the 32-year bone half-life and 96% skeletal body burden, the paediatric chelation figure above 25 micrograms per decilitre, and the organophosphate cholinesterase percentage bands. The JAMA Network Open 2023 United States and Canada acetaminophen consensus statement and the CDC "Recommended Actions Based on Blood Lead Level" page were not read, since neither is available as Europe PMC full text. No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
